description: Harden the existing publish.yml workflow with security best practices: pin all GitHub Actions to full SHA hashes (latest versions) instead of mutable tags, pin pnpm to a specific version instead of 'latest', and keep the existing permissions block.
steps: Change 'version: latest' under pnpm/action-setup to 'version: 9' (deterministic, avoids surprise breakage from new major versions)
NOTE: Do NOT add NODE_AUTH_TOKEN - the workflow uses NPM trusted publishing via OIDC (id-token: write). This is the correct, secure approach already in place.
Keep the existing permissions block (contents: read, id-token: write) - it is correct for trusted publishing
acceptance_criteria: All actions in publish.yml use full 40-character SHA pinning with a comment showing the version tag
pnpm version is pinned to a specific major version (not 'latest')
No NODE_AUTH_TOKEN is added - trusted publishing via OIDC is already the correct approach
verification: Read .github/workflows/publish.yml and confirm all 'uses:' lines have SHA-pinned references with version comments
findings: All three actions pinned to SHA with version comments. pnpm version set to 9. No NODE_AUTH_TOKEN added - trusted publishing via OIDC already in place. YAML validated.
